prd.title: Freelancer Task Management App
prd.overview: A task management application purpose-built for freelancers who juggle multiple clients, projects, and deadlines simultaneously. Unlike generic task tools, this app organises work around clients and projects, surfaces revenue-relevant context alongside tasks, and adapts to the non-linear, self-directed nature of freelance work.

goals.description: Give freelancers a single place to track tasks across all clients and projects, eliminating the need to maintain separate lists per client or tool.

goals.goal: Make deadlines and priorities visible at a glance
goals.description: Surface upcoming deadlines, overdue items, and priority conflicts without requiring manual triage each day.
Link tasks to billable projects so freelancers can see which work is paid, track hours against budgets, and flag scope creep early.
Support non-standard schedules — irregular hours, time zones, and day-to-day reprioritisation — without imposing rigid workflows.
Automate recurring task creation, reminders, and status updates so freelancers spend time on billable work rather than managing their task list.

user_stories.action: create a task and assign it to a client and project
user_stories.benefit: so that all my work is organised by who it is for and not just by topic

user_stories.action: set a due date and priority level on each task
user_stories.benefit: so that I know what to work on first when I start my day

user_stories.action: see a unified inbox of all tasks across all clients
user_stories.benefit: so that nothing falls through the cracks when I am working for multiple clients simultaneously

user_stories.action: log time against a task and see it measured against a project budget
user_stories.benefit: so that I can identify when a project is approaching its hour limit and have an informed conversation with the client

user_stories.action: create recurring tasks on a schedule I define
user_stories.benefit: so that regular obligations such as weekly reports or monthly invoices are created automatically without manual entry

user_stories.action: tag tasks as billable or non-billable
user_stories.benefit: so that I can accurately report hours to clients and exclude internal admin from invoices

user_stories.action: view a timeline or calendar view of tasks across all projects
user_stories.benefit: so that I can spot scheduling conflicts and avoid over-committing across clients

user_stories.action: archive a project and all its tasks when work is complete
user_stories.benefit: so that my active workspace stays uncluttered while historical work remains searchable

user_stories.action: receive a daily digest of tasks due today and overdue items
user_stories.benefit: so that I start each working day with a clear, prioritised list without having to build it manually

user_stories.action: share a read-only project task board with a client
user_stories.benefit: so that clients can see progress without needing to email me for status updates

user_stories.action: add notes and file attachments to a task
user_stories.benefit: so that all context for a piece of work is in one place and I do not lose track of briefs or reference materials

user_stories.action: filter and sort tasks by client, project, due date, or priority
user_stories.benefit: so that I can quickly focus on a single client engagement when needed

success_metrics.target: 70% of new users create at least one task and assign it to a project within their first session
60% of active users open the app at least 4 days per week
50% of users who complete onboarding return and create a task in week 4
40% of active users log time against at least one task per week within 60 days of signup
55% of active users have tasks across 2 or more active clients within 30 days
NPS of 40 or above at the 90-day cohort mark
Users mark at least 65% of created tasks as complete (vs abandoned), indicating tasks reflect real work rather than aspirational lists
30% of active users set up at least one recurring task within 45 days, reducing manual admin
